title: Every Aave instance receives the identical 50 million cap and 25 million per day slope, so the limits express a policy default rather than a per-counterparty risk measurement
content:
All four Aave instances carry the same numbers: `maxAmount` 50 million and `slope` 25 million per day on deposits, and `Unlimited` on withdrawals (A...5.1.2.4, A...5.2.2.4, A...5.3.2.4, A...5.4.2.4). Only the denominating asset changes.

If the limits were derived from a risk model, four instances with different collateral profiles, different market depth and different asset issuers would not converge on one number. A uniform envelope indicates a **standard starting allocation**: a default that is safe enough to apply broadly, applied uniformly until something justifies deviating.

That reading is consistent with the RRC status on each of these instances, which is `Pending` (A...5.1.1, A...5.2.1, A...5.3.1, A...5.4.1) — by the Atlas's own definition, the Instance Financial RRC is not yet calculated from a fully implemented risk model. There is no calibration available to differentiate them, so a default is the honest choice.

The two-day refill implied by the 50/25 pair is the substantive part of the default. It means a full drawdown of the budget cannot be repeated for two days, which is the property that buys human response time, and it is what makes a uniform figure defensible in the absence of per-counterparty modelling.

What to watch is whether these numbers stay identical once the risk models land. Uniform limits that persist after calibration becomes available would mean the RRC framework is not feeding back into the parameters it is supposed to inform.
description: The same envelope is applied to Aave Core v3 and to the structurally different Horizon RWA market, in each case denominated in that instance's own asset.
